cf.title: Include schema-qualified names in publication error messages (generalised to all of LR).

input.subject: Include schema-qualified names in publication error messages.

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal, and the demand objections were refuted. Three fixable design points remain at level 2: no written rule for which messages qualify names (prior-attempts-1), the unstated fate of the pushed RelationGetQualifiedRelationName() (maintenance-fit-1), and the open pg_temp versus pg_temp_N choice (maintenance-fit-3). None needs a different proposal, but a committer in this area has to settle them. The code was not read.

brief.title: Schema-qualified relation names in all logical replication messages
brief.problem: Many logical replication error and log messages name a relation without its schema, which is ambiguous when the same name exists in several schemas. Other messages build the qualified name by hand, or quote it twice inside a message that already supplies quotes. Users and administrators reading these messages are the ones affected.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0001 adds three helpers in relcache.c that return an unquoted "schema.relation" string for %s substitution, and converts every logical replication call site to use them, including index names. Patch 0002 removes get_qualified_objname() and inlines it into generate_qualified_relation_name() in ruleutils.c. The entry extends an earlier pushed EXCEPT-clause fix and Vignesh's v8 for check_publication_add_relation().
user_visible_surface: Text of about 20 logical replication error, detail and log messages changes: relations, tables, sequences and indexes appear as schema.relation.
Messages that used "%s.%s" change to a single "%s", so translations go fuzzy.
Temporary tables appear with schema pg_temp_N in these messages.
C API: new MsgQualifiedRelName(), MsgQualifiedRelNameByRel(), MsgQualifiedRelNameByRelId() in relcache.c.
author_claims: The same name lookup is done ad hoc in three inconsistent ways across more than a dozen logical replication call sites.
Unqualified names are ambiguous in routine per-schema publication setups.
Commit 926627bf902 shows that double quoting already caused a real bug.
Per the error style guide, the helpers should not quote, because the messages supply quotes.
Translator cost is low early in the v20 cycle, since gettext marks changed strings fuzzy and keeps the old translation.
brief.thread_state: The first part, for the EXCEPT clause, was pushed for v19; Vignesh's v8 for check_publication_add_relation() waits, and he wanted the wider change in a separate thread. Kuroda gave +1 to the idea but raised translator cost and preferred pg_temp over pg_temp_N; nobody else has reviewed the generalised patches.
unclear: The material does not show the full list of converted messages or which ones still print names unqualified.
No decision on pg_temp versus pg_temp_N for temporary tables, or how regression tests stay stable with pg_temp_N.
Euler objected to changing existing message text because log analysis tools depend on it; the thread does not settle whether that applies to HEAD.
The patch does not say how it relates to Amit's pushed RelationGetQualifiedRelationName() or whether that function is kept or replaced.
No statement on whether messages outside logical replication should follow the same rule.

prior_attempts.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
prior_attempts.quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 changed deparsed SQL at one ruleutils.c call site. This patch changes error and log message text through shared helpers across many call sites, but it defines its scope by subsystem.

prior_attempts.title: Explicit relation name in VACUUM VERBOSE log
prior_attempts.quote: Repeating the full table name in every line will be really annoying for that primary use-case.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane objected that VACUUM VERBOSE output is meant for people reading it in the client, and repeating the full table name on every line would be annoying for that use. He also said scraping INFO messages is a poor workflow, since translation changes them. Robert Haas doubted that qualifying names everywhere was useful and noted that the scope had grown. Daniel Gustafsson returned the patch because these concerns stayed open and the patch had no update during the commitfest.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 qualified names on every VACUUM VERBOSE line read in a client. This patch changes single-line error and log messages, where the name is not repeated.

objections.title: Two relation-name helpers with opposite quoting rules
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch author needs a qualified name for an errmsg and finds RelationGetQualifiedRelationName() next to MsgQualifiedRelNameByRel() in relcache.c. They pick the quoting one inside "%s", and the double-quote bug fixed by 926627bf902 comes back. No test or build check catches it.
objections.argument: Message #28 placed a quoting helper in relcache.c, and message #31 pushed it. Patch 0001 adds three non-quoting helpers in the same file, and 0002 removes only get_qualified_objname(). The proposal does not say whether RelationGetQualifiedRelationName() is kept, renamed or replaced. Two near-identical helpers that differ only in quoting are the API shape most likely to be misused.
objections.author_must_show: Is RelationGetQualifiedRelationName() removed or redefined by this series, and how would a new caller know which helper fits an errmsg?

critic.reasoning: Message #37 removes get_qualified_objname() but does not say what happens to the pushed RelationGetQualifiedRelationName(). Without the code, the material cannot show that only one helper remains for message use.

objections.title: Logical replication boundary gives no rule for which messages qualify names
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs `alter table` on a published table and gets a tablecmds.c error naming "public.t". A later error from the same command, outside logical replication, names it as "t". A future patch adds a new logical replication message with RelationGetRelationName(), and no test or check catches it.
objections.argument: [P5] was returned after reviewers asked for a defined rule on which call sites qualify names, backed by a documented helper; its reason is an AI summary, so it is only a pointer. Here the patch converts messages in shared files such as tablecmds.c, objectaddress.c and execReplication.c because they mention publications, not because of a general rule. The brief notes there is no statement for messages outside logical replication, and message #33 shows matview errors with the same double-quoting left as is. Message #38 lists four kinds of call sites kept unqualified by judgement.
objections.author_must_show: What written rule tells a future patch author whether a new message must use MsgQualifiedRelName(), and why does it stop at logical replication?

precedents.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled

critic.reasoning: The proposal states no rule beyond "all LR call sites", and message #38 shows the kept exceptions rest on judgement. [P5] concerns deparsed SQL in ruleutils.c, so it is only a weak pointer and must not be used as support.

objections.title: pg_temp_N makes temp-table messages untestable by text
objections.failure_scenario: A regression test hits one of the converted messages with a temporary table. The output contains pg_temp_N, which differs by backend, so the test fails at random. The test then falls back to VERBOSITY sqlstate and stops checking the message text.
objections.argument: Message #36 already had to switch a publication test to sqlstate-only output for this reason. Patch 0001 extends the same behaviour to about 20 messages and keeps pg_temp_N. Message #38 asked for pg_temp, and the thread has no decision. Each future test on these paths carries the same workaround.
objections.author_must_show: Which display of temp schemas is chosen, and how do regression tests for the converted messages keep checking message text?

critic.reasoning: Message #36 shows a core test already dropped its text check because of pg_temp_N, and message #37 leaves the choice open. The author calls it a one-line change, but the thread has no decision yet.

refuted.title: Logical replication gets its own naming rule with no project-wide rule
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs `refresh materialized view concurrently "my matv1"` and sees `"public."my matv1""`, while a publication error on the same kind of name shows `"public.my matv1"`. Later patches outside logical replication have no rule to tell them which helper to use or whether to qualify at all.
refuted.argument: The patch adds MsgQualifiedRelName*() helpers that do not quote, next to the pushed RelationGetQualifiedRelationName(), and the material does not say whether that function stays. Message #33 shows other backend messages already print nested quotes, so the patch creates a second convention instead of one documented rule. [P5] was returned partly because a reviewer asked for a defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper. Message #12 also asked for a common path, not one per subsystem.
refuted.author_must_show: What single rule for qualifying and quoting relation names in messages should the whole backend follow, and which helper should non-replication code use?

precedents.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1 for the missing rule and of maintenance-fit-1 for the two helpers. The matview nested quoting in its scenario exists today and is not caused by this patch.

refuted.title: pg_temp_N makes temporary-table error text change between runs
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension or application test suite hits one of the converted errors on a temporary table, and the expected output shows `pg_temp_14.t` on one run and `pg_temp_3.t` on the next. The test fails at random, and the only workaround in the material is hiding the message with `\set VERBOSITY sqlstate`.
refuted.argument: Message #36 shows the core regression test already had to stop checking the message text for this reason. Message #38 prefers `pg_temp`, and message #37 leaves the choice open. The proposal extends the unstable form to about 20 messages without deciding the question, and every downstream test that covers these paths pays for it.
refuted.author_must_show: Which form, pg_temp or pg_temp_N, do these messages print, and how do regression tests check the message text with that form?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-3, which rests on the core regression test evidence in message #36.

refuted.title: General helper, but the qualification rule covers only logical replication
refuted.failure_scenario: After commit, LR messages print schema.relation while tablecmds.c, matview.c and vacuum messages for the same table print a bare name. The next author outside LR does not know whether to qualify. Each later patch repeats the same discussion.
refuted.argument: The helpers live in relcache.c, so they are project-wide API, but the stated rule is "all LR call sites". Message #12 and message #26 already point to users outside LR. In [P5], a committer asked for a defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper, and judged a narrow patch too small. A committer would likely ask for that rule here before a subsystem-only convention is fixed in place.
refuted.author_must_show: What rule says which error messages, in any subsystem, should qualify relation names, and where is it documented for future authors?

precedents.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which makes the same point with the message #38 exceptions as evidence.

refuted.title: New message helpers sit beside the pushed RelationGetQualifiedRelationName()
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer later adds a logical replication error and picks RelationGetQualifiedRelationName() or generate_qualified_relation_name(), not the new MsgQualifiedRelName*(). If that helper quotes its output, the message double-quotes, which is the bug 926627bf902 fixed. Nothing fails loudly, so a reviewer finds out only from a user's log.
refuted.argument: Message #31 pushed RelationGetQualifiedRelationName() in relcache.c for this exact purpose. Message #37 adds three more relcache.c helpers and removes get_qualified_objname(), but does not say whether the pushed function is kept, renamed or replaced. Euler (message #26) pointed at matview.c, and message #33 shows REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW double-quoting today, so the right helper matters outside logical replication too. [P5] was returned partly because reviewers wanted one defined rule and a documented helper for name qualification, not more call-site variants.
refuted.author_must_show: Does 0001 replace RelationGetQualifiedRelationName(), and which single documented helper should new error messages anywhere in the backend use?

precedents.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. [P5] concerns ruleutils.c deparse output and does not support a point about message helpers.

refuted.title: No user report shows unqualified names confuse anyone in these messages
refuted.failure_scenario: About 20 logical replication messages change text in v20 because of an ambiguity no user has reported. Translators and log tool owners absorb the change. The project cannot point to any user whose problem it solved.
refuted.argument: Message #15 says no bug report has arrived, and message #16 calls it "a rare error-case scenario" that went unreported for a long time. Message #37 asserts per-schema publications are "routine" but cites no report from -general or -bugs. The pushed EXCEPT fix had a specific trigger, the new EXCEPT clause, as message #18 notes. The generalised patch has no such trigger. In [P1], Robert Haas doubted that qualifying names everywhere was useful once the scope grew beyond the original case.
refuted.author_must_show: Which -general or -bugs reports, or which production cases, show users misreading these specific logical replication messages because the schema was missing?

precedents.title: Explicit relation name in VACUUM VERBOSE log

critic.reasoning: In message #15 a committer calls the current behaviour not correct, and a worker log line that names only "t" gives the reader no other way to find the schema. [P1] concerns repeated VACUUM VERBOSE lines read in a client, which is a different case.

refuted.title: Message churn falls on log tools and translators, not on feature users
refuted.failure_scenario: After upgrading to v20, a team's log alert matches "cannot update table "orders"" from execReplication.c and stops firing, because the text now reads "public.orders". The team finds out only when replica identity errors are missed.
refuted.argument: In message #19, Euler objects that changing existing visible messages breaks log analysis tools, and in message #38 Kuroda raises translator cost for about 20 strings. Message #39 addresses the translator cost but not the log tools. Message #34 reads Euler's objection as being about backpatching only, which leaves the HEAD question open. Clarity improves only for users who have duplicate names across schemas, but every installation that parses these logs sees the text change.
refuted.author_must_show: For HEAD, what is the case that the gain for users with duplicate names outweighs breaking text-matching on about 20 existing messages for everyone else?

critic.reasoning: Message #19 opens with "-1 for backpatching" and says "the target is v20", so the log tool concern was about back branches. Message #39 answers the translator cost, and message text changes in a major release are normal practice.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 adds three MsgQualifiedRelName*() helpers in relcache.c, and patch 0002 removes get_qualified_objname().

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The text of about 20 existing messages changes, and message #19 objects to backpatching; the target is v20.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Future logical replication messages must use the new helpers, and nothing fails when a new message prints a bare name.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the series keep, rename or remove RelationGetQualifiedRelationName(), and how does a new caller know which helper fits a message that already supplies quotes?
What written rule tells a future patch author whether a new message must use MsgQualifiedRelName(), and where is that rule documented?
Do the converted messages print pg_temp or pg_temp_N for temporary tables, and how do regression tests keep checking the message text?
Which logical replication messages still print unqualified names after patch 0001, and what is the reason for each exception listed in message #38?
Should messages outside logical replication, such as the matview errors in message #33, follow the same rule in a later patch?

committability.owner_note: Amit Kapila pushed the first part (message #31) but has not reviewed the generalised patches. The owner needs to know logical replication messages and the relcache.c helper conventions.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the text of about 20 messages, the translation update, and a helper API in relcache.c that later patches will copy. The risk is low and limited to error and log paths.
committability.author_follow_up: Peter Smith created the CommitFest entry on 2026-11-05 and answered the translator concern in message #39, which suggests he stays for fixes.

priority.reason: The change helps logical replication users who have the same relation name in several schemas, and it touches only error and log paths. The three open design points are small and can be settled in the existing thread.

provisional_note: Without the code, I could not check whether patch 0001 leaves one helper or two for message use, or which call sites remain unqualified. The full list of converted messages was not shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Explicit relation name in VACUUM VERBOSE log
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the schema name to the relation names in VACUUM VERBOSE messages, which today qualify only the first "vacuuming" line. Later replies discussed extending schema qualification to log messages in general, possibly behind a GUC.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that VACUUM VERBOSE output is meant for people reading it in the client, and repeating the full table name on every line would be annoying for that use. He also said scraping INFO messages is a poor workflow, since translation changes them. Robert Haas doubted that qualifying names everywhere was useful and noted that the scope had grown. Daniel Gustafsson returned the patch because these concerns stayed open and the patch had no update during the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Repeating the full table
name in every line will be really annoying for that primary use-case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Mention column name in error messages
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the target column name to errors raised when a value cannot be coerced to a column's type in INSERT or ALTER COLUMN, for example "value too long for type character varying(4)". After review, the first version, which changed datatype input functions, was reworked to use an error context callback in the parser.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund reviewed the patch and asked for code cleanups and tests, since the patch had none. The author did not reply, and Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback two months after that review because the comments had not been addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Patch is marked as returned with feedback, it has been two months
since the last review, and comments have not been addressed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_stat_statements query jumbling to use relation name instead of relation oid
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Julien Rouhaud, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_stat_statements query jumbling to hash the relation name instead of the relation OID, so a queryid stays the same after a table is dropped and re-created. The author wanted stable, name-based queryids for use in other extensions such as pgaudit and sql_firewall.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan opposed the change, since renaming a table does not make it a different table. Julien Rouhaud and Michael Paquier noted that the patch ignores the schema (and the database), and that renames would change the queryid. Tom Lane said the idea only works if every OID in the jumble (types, operators, functions) is replaced by a name, and that the extra name lookups could cost much performance, so he voted to reject.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
That argument would only hold if *every* use of OIDs in the jumbles
were replaced by names --- not only tables, but types, operators,
functions, etc.  I'm already concerned that the additional name
lookups will cost a lot of performance, and I think adding so many
more would probably be disastrous.

precedents_retrieved.title: Mention column name in error messages
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the target column name and type to errors raised when a value is coerced into an insert or update column, such as "value too long for type character varying(4)". After review it used an error context callback set up during parse analysis of assigned expressions instead of changing datatype input functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found that the callback only covers errors raised during parse analysis or constant folding, not run-time errors from non-constant expressions, and covering those would need executor changes with a likely performance cost. He argued that partial coverage would mislead users and that the cases it handles already have error cursor information. He proposed extending error cursor support into execution instead, and Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it isn't,
we'd be best off to reject this patch rather than create an expectation
among users that such context should be there.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_get_constraintdef schema-qualify the referenced table in a foreign key's REFERENCES clause when pretty printing is off, as pg_get_indexdef already does. The goal is constraint definitions that can be recreated on another system with a different search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a clearly defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.

precedents_retrieved.title: simple decomposition of qualified identifier
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a SQL-callable function parse_ident() that splits a qualified identifier string into its parts (database, schema, object name), using the parsing that exists internally but is not exposed at the SQL level. Unlike a cast to regclass, it does not check that the object exists and does not use search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After the patch was marked ready for committer, Teodor Sigaev reported bugs in error handling. A carriage return is not escaped in the error message, the error for '.someTable' says "after" instead of "before", and long identifiers are truncated only when unquoted. The author said he would look at it, and Alvaro Herrera closed the entry as returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But, seems, there are some bugs in error processing.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move all am-related reloption code into src/backend/access/[am-name] and get rid of relopt_kind for custom AM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves reloption definitions out of reloptions.c into per-access-method option lists returned by a new amrelopt_catalog AM function, replaces amoptions, and puts generic option parsing into a new options.c. It also replaces StdRdOptions with per-relation-type structures, renames the Relation* macros, adds an enum option type, and rejects toast options on tables without a TOAST table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked that the patch be split, because the new tests and the TOAST table checks belonged in separate patches. Michael Paquier objected that the patch gives extensions no equivalent of add_int_reloption() and add_real_reloption(), and that the macro renames and other diff noise break APIs. The author did not post an update for two weeks, and then agreed to split the work into smaller patches.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There is still no API equivalent for add_int_reloption(),
add_real_reloption(), which is a problem as extension should be
allowed to still use that.

precedents_retrieved.title: NLS: use gettext() to translate system error messages
precedents_retrieved.summary: Translate the system error text substituted for %m with gettext and Postgres's own .po files, instead of relying on strerror_r() translation. This makes errno messages follow NLS on every platform and stops depending on LC_CTYPE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that platforms whose strerror() does not translate leave their users used to untranslated errno strings, so Postgres should behave like other programs on the platform. roaster_notes.note: The repetition concern in P1 does not apply to one-line errors. Only the scope-rule point from P5 still applies.
Euler's log-tool concern in message #19 was mainly about backpatching. For HEAD, changes to message text are routine, so I did not raise it as a separate objection.

The proposal changes only the text of server error and log messages and some backend helper functions; it adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or protocol state. Kuroda (message #38) confirms that replication protocol messages still send namespace and relation separately, so publishers, subscribers and mixed-version setups see no change. Removing get_qualified_objname(), which shipped in v19, is a normal major-release API change.

The proposal changes only how existing messages print a relation name, so it has no privilege or exposure aspect. The added schema names belong to relations the session already named or owns, or they appear in server logs that only administrators read.
No hot-path cost. These are error and log paths only. Amit Kapila, a committer in this area, engaged in the first part but has not yet reviewed the generalised patches.
